name: Postie Bike
summary: R123's Postie Bike: a bubbly Australian step-through delivery motorbike in the spirit of the 110 cc postie (generic: no Australia Post branding). A big raked leg shield, a front carrier with a mail tub, two postal-red panniers stacked with parcels, round mirrors and chunky little knobblies. The rider is part of the model: open-face white helmet, hi-vis vest over a blue work shirt. Code-built from a generated reference sheet (R81), on the bike part set (core, front, back, rider, wheel_F, wheel_R).
feedback: Comment on this page (what to change, which view or state); the session turns each comment into a bug bead that cites this page and the car's id.

reference.note: The reference sheets were generated with Muse Image from a written brief (art/vehicles/postie-bike/refs/prompts/), the Cruz Missile's sheet given as the layout example. Per view: the reference crop, the model shaded, and the silhouette diff (green is model only, red is reference only). Scored by tools/vehicles/fit (Spike J's method: perspective camera, the same mask pipeline on both sides, the contact-shadow band left out). Bikes are thin: the masks keep pale parts (segment.bright), use a small opening and keep detached components (refs/sheets.json), the same rules on both sides.

damage.note: Left to right: intact; front and back loose; the rider loose; wheel_F cambered; front detached; the rider thrown (detached, R121); back detached; wheel_F detached; rider and front detached; a stripped frame. Posed in a three.js viewer about each part's hinge line (tools/vehicles/evidence).

paints.pattern: Seat colour on the paint key (the leg shield, side covers and mudguards tint); the postal-red panniers, the hi-vis vest and the parcels keep their colours, so it reads as a postie in any seat colour. The number sits on the rider's back (anchor roof_number) and in the HUD badge.

inWorld.label: Own car in its tile, large (1 tile, TV 1080p; viewer, not the host renderer)
From the Derby overview camera (top-down damage row)

findings.text: contract + reproducibility (validator clean on the bike part set, origin on the ground between the axles, wheels on the centreline, anchors cam_fp, cam_tp_target, com, roof_number (the rider's back), lplate_front, lplate_rear; no badges, logos or real names)

silhouette: weighted IoU 0.813 for LOD0 against 'lod + 1' (side 0.829, top 0.900, front 0.701, rear 0.706); 0.674 for LOD2 against 'lowest' (side 0.534: that sheet's spoked wheels aren't filled in its mask, so the model's solid octagons count as extra). A bike's thin parts (forks, frame, arms) score lower than a car body; the cues read by eye

by-eye cues: leg shield, front carrier with the mail tub, the two postal-red panniers stacked with parcels, round mirrors, the hi-vis rider in a white helmet; at grid-24 it reads as a postie in every seat colour (the panniers and vest keep their colours)
paint key / one material (a flat swatch atlas; draws per tile are the bike's 6 parts, one InstancedMesh per part type; the renderer now keeps a bike's two wheels as their own types)
damage states (front and back hang about their hinge lines, the rider pitches off about the hip and is thrown when detached, a wheel comes off; no interior bays: a bike has no panels to open)
physics fit (a convex proxy per part from the bake, colliders.png; the profile's geometry synced from the sidecar)
detail: the leg shield reads as a thin raked plank from the side; the exhaust sits low like a skid; LOD2 drops the exhaust and grips to keep a parcel a side

accel.note: engine force over mass at launch: an upper bound, drag and traction not included

topSpeed.note: Not measured yet: the bike profiles join the roster (and the R122 handling bank and fun tests) once the R136 handling schema lands; R123's balance bead (br-bwju.6) measures every vehicle's speed, launch and cornering on real maps.
